# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Economic Policy
The manifesto proposes cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027 and abolishing self-employed National Insurance entirely. The party commits to not raising income tax, VAT, or corporation tax. A "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure state pensions and pensioner tax allowances rise annually by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%.

## Taxation and Families
Child Benefit thresholds would shift to household-based assessment, with withdrawal beginning at £120,000 combined income. Working parents would receive 30 hours of free childcare weekly from nine months until school age.

## Immigration
A legal cap on migration would be introduced with annual parliamentary votes. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue for illegal migrants. Visa fees would increase, and health checks would be required for incoming migrants.

## Defence and Security
Defence spending would reach 2.5% of GDP by 2030. The manifesto commits to continued Ukraine support, nuclear deterrent modernisation, and increased domestic munitions production.

## Housing
The target is 1.6 million new homes, with permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000. A new Help to Buy scheme would provide 20% equity loans.

## Health and Education
NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Mobile phones would be banned in schools. A new "Advanced British Standard" would reform 16-19 education.

## Energy and Environment
Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing would continue. The party commits to net zero by 2050 while guaranteeing no new green levies. Nuclear power expansion includes Small Modular Reactors.

## Transport
The £2 bus fare cap would continue. £36 billion from HS2 savings would fund regional transport projects. The manifesto opposes road pricing and would reverse London's ULEZ expansion.
